name: IEC open-circuit output, L-type (open collector)
summary: Underlined diamond inside an outline: an open-circuit output that can only drive a low level.
description: The underlined diamond marks an output, such as an NPN open collector or an N-channel open drain, that can supply a relatively low-impedance L level when on and is open when off. An external pull-up is needed. TI's public overview notes this output type supports a positive-logic wired-AND connection.

When a variant with a built-in passive pull-up exists, a further mark inside the diamond distinguishes it. Reviewing the exact qualifier tells the drafter whether an external pull-up must be added to the schematic.
The qualifier does not state the maximum pull-up voltage. Some open-drain outputs tolerate a higher pull-up rail than the device supply and some do not.
readingNotes: Underline below the diamond: pulls low only.
Find the external pull-up on the net.
drawingChecklist: Draw the diamond with its underline next to the output.
distinction: The H-type open-circuit output has the line above the diamond and drives a high level only.
